# Crate index

<p class="pm-kind"><b>Reference · generated</b> · every workspace crate by tier, with the description its manifest carries</p>

A tier depends only on the tiers below it; the peripheral surface depends on all of them and is depended on by none. The description column is each crate's `Cargo.toml` description, so this table is exactly what `cargo metadata` reports. The status column is the crate's `package.metadata.pulse-mesh.status`: `pre-integration` for a crate the tree ships but does not use yet (ADR-0014), `partial` for one in use some of whose public entry points return a deferred error (ADR-0017), blank for one that is finished and wired in.

## The canonical primitive (tier 0, `pulse/`)

| Crate | Path | Status | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `gen-test-vectors` | `pulse/pulse-spec/tools/gen-test-vectors` |  | Regenerate the language-neutral conformance fixtures under test-vectors/. |
| `mesh-capability` | `pulse/mesh-capability` |  | Pulse Mesh capability negotiation: per-node feature flags + version negotiation handshake. |
| `mesh-context` | `pulse/mesh-context` | pre-integration | Pulse Mesh Context Registry / Book of Standards: 16-bit context_id + 16-bit subscope namespace partitioning of the Pulse scope field. |
| `mesh-lex` | `pulse/mesh-lex` |  | Pulse Mesh public conformance substrate — minimum-viable lex registry + Merkle root over the registered catalog. |
| `pulse-canon` | `pulse/pulse-canon` |  | Pulse Mesh canonical primitive: the 128-byte Pulse + PulseEnvelope codec + NodeId. Tier 0 (the shape). |

## The engine (tier 1, `core/`)

| Crate | Path | Status | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `core-backoff` | `core/core-backoff` |  | Pulse Mesh backoff for OS-visible stalls: spin, then yield, then sleep in fixed steps. Tier 1 (the engine). |
| `core-region` | `core/core-region` |  | Pulse Mesh shared-memory mechanism (shm_open, size and reserve, mmap, unlink), NUMA placement (hugepage backings, mbind, thread pinning) and PulseRegion, the single-slot region. Tier 1 (the engine). |
| `core-ring` | `core/core-ring` |  | Pulse Mesh SHM-backed SeqLock ring buffer (single-writer, N-reader). Tier 1 (the engine). |
| `core-store` | `core/core-store` |  | Pulse Mesh EnvelopeStore: SHM circular buffer for variable-size envelopes with content-addressed lookup. Tier 1 (the engine). |
| `core-transport` | `core/core-transport` |  | Pulse Mesh PulseSender / PulseReceiver trait family. Substrate-agnostic transport contract. Tier 1 (the engine). |
| `mesh-stage-registry` | `core/mesh-stage-registry` |  | Compile-time stage / function registry macro for ring hubs. The `register_stages!` macro enumerates a hub's functions and stages and emits RING_MANIFEST, so the inner-ring four-crate composition is asserted in source and testable. |
| `pms-crc32c` | `core/pms-crc32c` |  | Pulse Mesh CRC32C trailer: compute and verify the checksum a Pulse carries in its last four bytes. Module M10. Tier 1 (the engine). |
| `pulse-wire-udp` | `core/pulse-wire-udp` |  | UDP framing for the Pulse Mesh Standard wire transport: one Pulse + variable-size envelope per datagram, MTU-aware, CRC32C-protected, with optional backpressure, NACK retransmission and FEC. |

## The peripheral surface (tier peripheral, `tools/`, `examples/`)

| Crate | Path | Status | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `example-01-hello-pulse-rust` | `examples/01-hello-pulse-rust` |  | Example 01 — encode + decode a PulseEnvelope, print its BLAKE3 content hash. |
| `example-02-loopback-udp-rust` | `examples/02-loopback-udp-rust` |  | Example 02 — a sender and a receiver thread exchanging Pulses over UDP loopback in one process. |
| `example-03-embed-ring-rust` | `examples/03-embed-ring-rust` |  | Example 03 — the shared-memory ring and the envelope store used directly, without the daemon. |
| `gen-lex-root` | `tools/gen-lex-root` |  | Regenerate the published lex_root (pulse/pulse-spec/lex-root.txt) for the current public mesh-lex registry state, into the path given. |
| `pulse-cli` | `tools/pulse-cli` |  | The standard's own command line, `pulse`: encode, decode and verify envelopes, send and receive Pulses over UDP, and the loopback smoke bench, over pulse-canon and pulse-wire-udp alone. Peripheral. |
